New York's Democratic governor has appointed a special prosecutor in the case of a woman who says she was gang-raped at the Cornell University fraternity in 2024.
As Steve Kastenbaum reports, the investigation was initially closed without any charges brought.
Governor Kathy Hochul says the young woman was failed by the people obligated to protect her.
I will not allow anyone to sweep this case under the rug.
We are ensuring that all the facts of this case are brought into the light.
It will now be up to State Attorney General Letitia James to determine whether any of the seven accused fraternity members will face criminal charges.
We will review the facts, gather evidence, interview witnesses, and if warranted, pursue prosecutions.
The governor says she lost faith in the local prosecutor's ability to handle the case.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Kastenbaum in New York.
A federal judge has ordered all border-related construction to stop immediately in Texas' Big Bend region, including in Big Bend National Park.
As Marfa Public Radio's Mary Cantrell reports, the emergency injunction will remain in effect while a lawsuit moves forward.
The Center for Biological Diversity, a church restoration group, and a river guide are suing the federal government over its border wall plans.
The judge's order says the Big Bend region is not necessarily an area of high legal entry, as federal waivers fast-tracking the project have claimed.
Anti-wall advocates, including Susan Hayes, celebrated outside of a federal courthouse in El Paso.
The government had no justification legally to issue the waivers in the first place.
It's what we all knew, to say that there is an emergency with immigration or border security and the greater Big Bend is complete and utter yes.
If the Trump administration appeals, the case will go to the U.S. Supreme Court.
For NPR News, I'm Mary Cantrell in El Paso.
The average price of jet fuel hit a new high last month, and PR's Jill Rose has more on our story.
The average price for a gallon of jet fuel climbed to $4.37 in September, according to the tracking firm Argus.
Airlines for America, the industry trade group that represents the major airlines, says that sets a new all-time high, narrowly eclipsing the previous record set in April, shortly after the war in Iran began.
The group says airlines are cutting flights and retiring older aircraft to keep costs down, but carriers are also passing some of their fuel costs on to the consumer. The average domestic airfare has reached its highest point of the year, according to the travel website Kayak, at more than $400, with the holiday travel season looming.
Joel Rose, NPR News, Washington.
Stocks finished the week up across the board. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up by half a percent. The NASDAQ closed up 1.2 percent. The S&P 500 was up three-quarters of a percent. This is NPR News.
CBS and the NFL star turned commentator Tony Romo have parted ways. The move follows Romo's arrest this summer for operating a vehicle while intoxicated. NPR's Becky Sullivan has more.
Back in July, Romo was arrested in Wisconsin after he performed poorly on field sobriety tests. Police said he had been the lead game analyst for CBS's NFL coverage since 2017. And that gig, of course, followed his decade-plus-long career as quarterback for the Dallas Cowboys.
After the arrest, Romo apologized and said the multiple back surgeries that ended his career prematurely have left him with "constant debilitating pain," which led to a reliance on pain medication, and attempts to buck that dependence, he says, led to problems with alcohol.
In a new statement, CBS said the decision to part ways with Romo was mutual. In Romo's absence this season, the former Houston Texans star J.J. Watt has been filling in. CBS says Watt will continue in the role. Becky Sullivan, NPR News.
South Korea says North Korea fired at least one ballistic missile toward the sea on Saturday. The launch took place on that country's eastern coast. The situation between the two countries has been tense because of landmine blasts in the demilitarized zone earlier this year that injured three South Korean soldiers. The South has now increased surveillance in case of additional launches.
Widespread student protests are continuing in France this weekend. Officials say there have been thousands of arrests since the protests began last week and hundreds of injuries have been reported. The students are demonstrating against under-resourced schools in the complex university entrance systems.
The Education Ministry says the protests have now reached about 560 schools. I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
